calls.title: T-Mobile<>GrowthBook - Project Discussion
calls.summary:
# MEDDICC Sales Call Summary

Call on [date not specified] with Jake Heier and Logan (GrowthBook account and technical team) and Steve Hamilton, Ramesh, and James Goudreault (T-Mobile).

## Attendees and Titles
Steve Hamilton and Ramesh represented T-Mobile's advanced analytics data science organization, positioned at headquarters in Seattle. James Goudreault joined as a product manager, also headquartered. Jake Heier served as GrowthBook's account lead, with Logan as technical counterpart. The call included multiple additional T-Mobile product managers invited but attendance was uncertain.

## Current State and Pain Points
T-Mobile currently lacked formal, broad-based experimentation processes despite having feature flagging primarily for operational release validation. The organization did not conduct systematic A/B testing across product teams. Some isolated testing occurred within AI and engineering functions for specific model behaviors, but this remained ad-hoc and departmentalized. James confirmed no formalized product team-driven experimentation existed, though a new data science partnership aimed to establish experimentation as a core team value and goal.

## Technical Requirements
T-Mobile explicitly prioritized self-hosting solutions due to privacy and compliance considerations. The organization had existing infrastructure investments in Databricks and Snowflake, requiring seamless integration capabilities. Additionally, Claude support and MCP (Model Context Protocol) functionality were identified as valuable tools for internal analysis workflows.

## Budget Authority and Decision Process
The call did not reveal explicit budget authority or signing power. However, the involvement of both product and data science leadership suggested multi-stakeholder decision-making. The unsigned NDA indicated the deal remained in preliminary exploration stages, with specific project details deferred pending formalization.

## Quantifiable Outcomes and ROI Signals
Steve articulated a compelling historical precedent from his e-commerce background at drugstore.com, where systematic A/B testing became standard for every software release. He described the methodology: form hypothesis, rollout to 5%, measure for one week, scale to 25-50% if successful, then full population release. This demonstrated mature experimentation thinking and expected measurable impact, though specific T-Mobile metrics weren't quantified during this call.

## Champion Signals
Steve Hamilton emerged as the primary champion, bringing direct experimentation experience and clear methodology preferences. His enthusiasm for gradual rollout techniques and specific technical requirements suggested serious evaluation intent. James Goudreault's involvement signaled product team buy-in for potential implementation.

## Competitors and Alternatives
No competitors were mentioned. T-Mobile's current state involved building internal solutions rather than evaluating established platforms, representing a greenfield opportunity.

## Decision Timeline and Next Steps
The call focused on discovery rather than immediate next steps. Jake proposed understanding current experimentation processes, identifying specific A/B testing requirements, and potentially delivering a broad platform overview and demonstration. The unsigned NDA suggested immediate action items included NDA execution and scheduling follow-up technical discussions around Databricks/Snowflake integration capabilities and Claude/MCP support specifics.
